== Exercise 1 ==

Calculate (when it exists) the matrix product $M = M_1 M_2$ with:

1.
$$
M_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}, \quad M_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}
$$

2.
$$
M_1 = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 2 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad M_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

3.
$$
M_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 4 & 16 \\ 45 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad M_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}
$$

4.
$$
M_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad M_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

5.
$$
M_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad M_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}
$$

== Exercise 2 ==

Let $A$ and $B$ be two square matrices:

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \end{pmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

Calculate the result of the following operations:

1. $\det(A)$, $\det(B)$, $A^T$, $B^T$.

2. $A^{-1}$. Deduce the comatrix of $A$.

Reminder:
$$
A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det(A)} \operatorname{com}(A)
$$

3. $AB$, $BA$, and $A+B$.

4. $A^2 + AB + BA + B^2$ and $A^2 + 2AB + B^2$ with $A^2 = AA$. Conclude.

== Exercise 3 ==

1. Calculate the scalar product of the vectors
$$
\vec{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 6 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \quad \text{and} \quad \vec{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}
$$
using several methods.

2. Calculate the norm of the vector
$$
\vec{w} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}
$$
using several methods.

== Exercise 4 ==

A mining company operates three deposits and extracts three minerals $A$, $B$, and $C$, whose three main constituents $a$, $b$, and $c$ are identical, but whose grades vary such that:

* 1000 tonnes of $A$ contain 600 tonnes of $a$, 200 tonnes of $b$, and 100 tonnes of $c$.
* 1000 tonnes of $B$ contain 700 tonnes of $a$, 100 tonnes of $b$, and 150 tonnes of $c$.
* 1000 tonnes of $C$ contain 700 tonnes of $a$, 150 tonnes of $b$, and 50 tonnes of $c$.

The company must produce in one month 20000 tonnes of $a$, 5000 tonnes of $b$, and 3000 tonnes of $c$, and seeks the respective quantities of the three minerals it must extract.

Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be the respective quantities of minerals $A$, $B$, and $C$ in thousands of tonnes that must be extracted.

Put the problem in matrix form and determine the quantities of minerals $A$, $B$, and $C$ required to meet the specifications.

== Exercise 5 ==

Let $f$ and $g$ be linear maps from $\mathbb{R}^3$ to $\mathbb{R}^3$ defined in the canonical bases by:

$$
f(x,y,z) = \begin{cases} x + 3z \\ x + y + 4z \\ 3x + 3z \end{cases}, \quad g(x,y,z) = \begin{cases} x - z \\ y \\ -x + y \end{cases}
$$

Determine, in matrix form, the following linear maps (in the canonical bases):

1. $p = g \circ f$

2. $q = f \circ g$

3. $m = p \cdot q$
